6
A person, travelling on a motorway a total distance of 200 km, travels the first 90 km at an
average speed of 80 km h–1.
Which average speed must be obtained for the rest of the journey if the person is to reach the
destination in a total time of 2 hours 0 minutes?
A
110 km h–1
B
120 km h–1
C
122 km h–1
D
126 km h–1

hints: Start with the first $90 \text{ km}$ at $80 \text{ km h}^{-1}$ and work out how much of the $2.0 \text{ h}$ total time it uses.
Subtract to find what is left for the second part: remaining distance from $200 - 90 = 110 \text{ km}$ and remaining time from $2.0 \text{ h}$ minus the first time.
Use $\text{average speed} = \text{distance} / \text{time}$ again for the remaining $110 \text{ km}$ and the remaining time in hours.
walkthrough: Total distance is $200 \text{ km}$ and total allowed time is $2.0 \text{ h}$. The first part is $s_1 = 90 \text{ km}$ at $v_1 = 80 \text{ km h}^{-1}$.
Use $t = s/v$ for the first part: $t_1 = 90/80 = 1.125 \text{ h}$.
Find what is left. Remaining distance $s_2 = 200 - 90 = 110 \text{ km}$. Remaining time $t_2 = 2.0 - 1.125 = 0.875 \text{ h}$.
Required average speed for the rest is $v_2 = s_2/t_2 = 110/0.875$.
Calculate: $v_2 \approx 125.7 \text{ km h}^{-1}$, which to the given options is about $126 \text{ km h}^{-1}$. This is option D.

A.explanation: This is the result of dividing the remaining $110 \text{ km}$ by $1.0 \text{ h}$, which ignores the $1.125 \text{ h}$ already used for the first $90 \text{ km}$.

B.explanation: This is close to simply averaging $80 \text{ km h}^{-1}$ and the required speed to get $100 \text{ km h}^{-1}$, but average speed depends on time spent at each speed, not a simple mean.

C.explanation: This is slightly low because of rounding the first section time to $1.1 \text{ h}$ instead of the exact $1.125 \text{ h}$, leaving too much time for the second section.

D.explanation: The remaining $110 \text{ km}$ must be covered in $0.875 \text{ h}$, giving $110/0.875 \approx 126 \text{ km h}^{-1}$.
